decisions.decision: The five _calc derivations move into analytics; telemetry loses the columns, deriveConsumption, and the five Snapshot port fields.
decisions.why: Rejected computing-on-read in telemetry: it leaves telemetry owning a derivation whose only consumer is another module, and taxes every read forever.

decisions.decision: Analytics gets the exact predecessor via a new telemetry port method SnapshotPrecedingDay, not a widened fixed lookback.
decisions.why: A gap longer than any fixed N yields a silently wrong delta that looks plausible on a chart, so nothing would ever flag it.

decisions.decision: Existing vehicle_metrics rows are rebuilt by deleting the vehicle_snapshots watermark in a migration; the next Reconcile backfills.
decisions.why: Reuses machinery tier 3 already built and the owner exercised. Avoids a second throwaway runner, which last time swept a 15MB binary into the repo.

decisions.decision: The change spans telemetry and analytics and needs two migrations, one per module; no sub-task edits both modules.
decisions.why: A telemetry migration must never write analytics' table. Preserves module data ownership while the derivation moves.

decisions.decision: Pulled the pre-existing SnapshotsByVehicleBetween LIMIT 400 truncation bug into this tier as task 4.9 (raise to 4000), against the worker's out-of-scope call.
decisions.why: I3 deliberately re-runs the full-history path that trips it, and truncation is silent while the watermark still advances. Re-arming a known silent-corruption bug is not minimal scope.

decisions.decision: Proceeded through the built-in database design gate without the owner's confirmation of the DDL and index plan.
decisions.why: Owner said 'autopilot ON for everything' and left after confirming I1-I4, the substantive calls. Everything stays local and unpushed, so it is vetoable; full DDL leads the audit.

decisions.decision: Wave 2 dispatched on Opus rather than the Sonnet default.
decisions.why: It is the tier correctness heart: moving a formula that must stay byte-for-byte identical, plus D8b, where under-widening the charge fetch yields a negative consumed_pct and a FALSE missing-charge alarm.

decisions.decision: Resolved D8b prose-vs-code contradiction in favour of the code: charge fetches widen on every call, not only across a gap.
decisions.why: The code block is normative and the design own rationale authorises generous over-fetching as result-neutral. Fixed the design and task 3.3 rather than let implementation quietly define the expectation.

decisions.decision: Ran waves 3 and 4 as two concurrent workers instead of the default single serial worker per wave.
decisions.why: Disjoint modules and disjoint files, and the bucket is at 68% with a 90% checkpoint - parallel buys a whole wave of progress before the owner has to resume anything.

decisions.decision: Wave 3 is forbidden from referencing the five _calc fields on telemetry.Snapshot.
decisions.why: Wave 4 deletes those fields concurrently. A wave-3 test constructing a Snapshot literal that sets them would break the build through no fault of either worker.

decisions.decision: Narrowed task 6a.1 from authoring the round-trip test to renaming and verifying the one wave 4 already wrote.
decisions.why: 4.8 and 6a.1 both claimed the same test. Narrowing removes duplicate work without weakening a criterion - all three cases are still required.

events.event: Tier 4 artifacts created by the telemetry worker and validated (openspec validate --changes --strict passes). The worker corrected SEVEN points in the leader's dispatch context; three that mattered were independently re-verified before acceptance: LIMIT 400 at query.sql:72 (real), PreviousSnapshotForVehicle already exists so I2 promotes a private seam rather than inventing a query (lowers risk), and deriveConsumption is at service.go:581 not :398 (leader was wrong). The worker also caught a timezone trap: reusing the existing query's captured_at < dayStart(...) bound would make a 03:30 Tokyo capture its own predecessor, so the new query bounds on captured_date < @day instead.

Wave 1 dispatched (telemetry, Sonnet, serial): add SnapshotPrecedingDay to the port. Purely additive - no column drops, no behaviour change - so it is the safe first wave and everything downstream depends on it. Budget at dispatch: five_hour 40%, context 15%.

Wave 1 COMPLETE (telemetry, additive). Worker found a gap tasks.md missed: widening the public telemetry.Reader breaks every fake of it repo-wide, not just in-module. Leader fixed the two gateway fakes itself (cross-module integration is the leader role, not a worker sandbox): fakeReader in handlers_test.go and fakeHistoryReader in history_test.go, each mirroring the precedent tier 3 set when it added SnapshotsByVehicleUpdatedSince. The worker reported only the first - go vet stops at one error per package - so the leader enumerated all implementers by grep instead of re-running vet iteratively. go vet is now clean except internal/analytics fakeTelemetryReader, which is wave 2 task 2.5 by design. Worker deviation accepted: it widened the store interface in service.go, outside the literal file list but inside its sandbox, because reader.store is statically typed and Go cannot widen an interface method set from another file; the alternative was a second parallel interface over an existing exactly-shaped seam.

Leader-owned integration fix outside any worker sandbox: internal/gateway/handlers/handlers_test.go and history_test.go gained SnapshotPrecedingDay stubs. design.md Non-Goals said no gateway change because no gateway code reads a _calc field - true, but it did not anticipate that widening the Reader interface itself breaks the gateway test-only mocks. The Non-Goal is narrowed, not violated.
Wave 2 dispatched (analytics, Opus, serial): the derivation moves in, plus D8b. Budget at dispatch: five_hour 54%, context 18%.

Wave 2 COMPLETE (analytics). The worker returned a truthful red signal instead of a convenient green: go vet ./internal/analytics/... still fails on 14 deriveVehicleMetrics call sites in consumed_test.go, because 2.2 changed the signature and tasks.md assigns those updates to 3.2, not 2.5. It declined to fix them, which would have silently executed half of another wave task. Correct call - accepted as-is, wave 3 clears it. The code block was right, the prose wrong. Corrected design.md D8b, the same wrong claim the worker had copied into recalculate.go comment, and task 3.3 expected value which was written from the withdrawn prose and would have failed against a correct implementation.
